newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SQUASH-IRVING ENDS MARTIN'S HOPES OF RECORD FOURTH TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-IRVING ENDS MARTIN'S HOPES OF RECORD FOURTH TITLE.

text.p: World number one Michelle Martin of Australia, seeking a record fourth successive World Open title, fell to a shock defeat by fifth seeded compatriot Liz Irving in the quarter-finals on Friday.
After leading 1-0 and 8-5 in the second game, the 29-year-old top seed fell into a completely uncharacteristic pattern of nervous errors that eventually led to her 46-minute 4-9 10-9 9-5 9-5 defeat.

"She gave me opportunities," said the 31-year-old Irving, a veteran of the women's circuit who has been playing World Open championships since she was a teenager, with her best result coming in 1993 when she reached the final before losing to Martin.
"I have had injury problems all year which I haven't talked about much and I have deliberately kept my head down here. But I am strong and in good shape and I was ready for the chances she game me."
And the chances were frequent. After clinching the 12-minute opening game 9-4 from 2-3 down, the Sydney-based defending champion advanced with some confidence to 8-5 and game ball.
But a momemtary hesitation covering a crisp backhand volley return of service for the game signalled the insecurity that was to lead to her downfall.
Irving, who beat Martin the last time they met on Malaysian soil, in the Malaysian Open final last year, then fought back to 9-9, benefiting from two unforced errors into the tin.
There was a prolonged tussle in the tiebreak but Irving held firm, taking the last two rallies with a cunningly contrived penalty stroke on the backhand and then a neat little drop shot.
Martin went 5-1 up in the third but then Irving struck a fierce forehand drive that rifled past Martin, triggering another run of four points and bringing three more unforced errors.
Another tussle at 5-5 led only to another Irving single hand run to 9-5, again finishing with a neat backhand drop.

The fourth was virtually a replay of the third but just more emphatic. Irving won at a canter from 1-5 down in a single hand, finishing on another backhand drop, this time across court and played at power.
Irving now goes in a semifinal against fourth seed Cassie Jackman of England, who beat Germany's Sabine Schone 9-2 9-2 9-4.
Second seed Sarah Fitz-Gerald of Australia beat compatriot Carol Owens 9-2 9-1 9-1 and will meet England's Sue Wright who defeated Suzanne Horner, also of England, 9-4 9-0 9-4.
